problem: The block diagram sends the SAR register straight into the comparator (dashed edge 'next trial'), with no internal DAC. The text in Section 2 correctly says the SAR code is turned into a voltage by a DAC before the comparator sees it, so the figure contradicts the explanation and teaches the wrong architecture.
fix: Insert a DAC block between the SAR register and the comparator: SAR register → DAC (trial voltage) → comparator, and comparator → SAR register carries the decision ('too high / too low'). The SAR register then feeds the output latch as drawn.

problem: 'eight comparison clocks plus internal overhead' suggests the overhead is small. In the ADC0808 the internal timing takes eight clock periods per bit, so 100 µs at 640 kHz is 64 clock periods, not about 8. A student multiplying 8 × 1.5625 µs gets 12.5 µs and is confused.
fix: Say: at 640 kHz one clock period is 1.5625 µs; the chip uses eight clock periods per bit, so 64 periods give the 100 µs conversion time. The SAR still needs only eight decisions, one per bit.

where: Exam traps, last trap (ALE and START)
problem: It says ALE and START are separate pulses and must be done in that order. On the ADC0808/0809 the two inputs may be tied together: the address latches on the rising edge of ALE and the conversion starts on the falling edge of START, which is why many 8086 interfacing circuits drive them from one port line.
fix: Keep the two-pulse sequence as one valid method, then add: ALE and START may also be tied together and driven from a single line, because the rising edge latches the address and the falling edge starts the conversion.

problem: 'Two numbers describe any DAC. The step size ... is Vref/256' is only true when Rf = R. With a different feedback resistor the step is Vref × (Rf/R)/256.
fix: Write: with Rf = R the step size (resolution in volts) is Vref/256 and full scale is Vref × 255/256; in general the step is Vref × (Rf/R)/256.

problem: 'a few hundred polls are normal' overstates the count. On an 8086 at a few MHz one pass (IN, test, jump) takes only a few microseconds, so a 100 µs conversion completes in roughly tens of polls, not hundreds.
fix: Say: each pass is one IN and one test; at 100 µs a conversion the loop runs a few dozen times.
